channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Iraq launches probe into alleged oil smuggling route to Afghanistan
item.description: Iraq's Parliament Speaker has ordered an investigation into intelligence reports alleging that petroleum from Kirkuk and the Kurdistan Region is being smuggled through Iran to Afghanistan. A temporary investigative committee has been established to examine the alleged route, which reportedly begins in oil-producing areas and extends toward Afghanistan via Iran.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan to cooperate on saiga population recovery and anti-poaching efforts
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan will collaborate to restore the saiga antelope population and combat poaching. This joint effort aims to protect the endangered species and ensure its long-term survival through coordinated conservation strategies and enforcement measures.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Editor and blogger sentenced to over 10 years in prison
item.description: A court in Tashkent has sentenced the head of Demokrat.uz, F.M., to 10 years and 3 months, and blogger A.G. to 10 years and 1 month in prison. They were found guilty of extortion, fraud, and illegal arms possession. The court also ordered F.M. to pay compensation to victims. The sentences can be appealed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Official Oversees Bishkek Heat and Power Plant Winter Readiness
item.description: Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Erlist Akunbekov, inspected the Bishkek Heat and Power Plant to assess its readiness for the 2026-2027 autumn-winter season. Discussions focused on reliable electricity production and continuous supply of heat and electricity to consumers.

item.title: New Tashkent to Get Its Own City Administration Following Presidential Decree
item.description: A presidential decree establishes a dedicated administration for New Tashkent, responsible for its management and services until a formal administrative-territorial unit is created. The administration will initially have 14 staff members, with additional personnel allocated to various government bodies within the new city.

item.title: Batken Authorities Address Issues Raised by 11 Citizens During Presidential Meeting
item.description: Work is underway in Kyrgyzstan's Batken region to resolve issues raised by 11 citizens during a meeting with President Sadyr Japarov. A working group reviewed their appeals, resolving some issues on the spot and tasking relevant agencies with addressing others within legal frameworks.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Government Expands Ministry of Economy's Powers Over Public Services
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has broadened the authority of the Ministry of Economy and Commerce concerning the provision of state and municipal services. The ministry will now shape unified policy, monitor service delivery standards, gauge citizen and business satisfaction, and develop rules for a non-application-based service format.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Editor Sentenced to Over 10 Years for Extortion and Fraud
item.description: Fazliddinkhon Mekhmonov, editor-in-chief of Demokrat.uz, has been sentenced to 10 years and 3 months in prison by a Tashkent court. He was found guilty of extortion, fraud, and illegal arms possession. Blogger Aziz Goipnazarov received a 10-year sentence for extortion. The court ordered Mekhmonov to pay material damages.

item.title: Preparations for Presidential Election Discussed in Kyrgyzstan's Batken Region
item.description: Preparations for the presidential election, including equipping polling stations and ensuring security, were discussed in Kyrgyzstan's Batken region. Regional officials reviewed the organization of district and city штабs, support for election commissions, and provision of electricity and internet. Tasks were assigned to verify voter lists and monitor campaign legality.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Man Sentenced to Three Years for Social Media Repost
item.description: Baktybek Moldaliev has been sentenced to three years in prison by an Osh court for reposting materials from publications previously declared extremist. Moldaliev claims he did not share the content online as his phone was confiscated by investigators. His wife stated the court did not consider his arguments.

item.title: Tajikistan to Discuss Digital Registration for Women Entrepreneurs via E-wallets
item.description: A roundtable in Dushanbe will discuss the digital registration of women entrepreneurs through e-wallets. The event, organized by the Association of E-commerce Participants of Tajikistan, will focus on a research project for self-employed women in e-commerce. Participants will explore legislative and technical limitations for a pilot project.

item.title: Relatives of 'Atajurt' activists report pressure and demand release
item.description: Relatives of convicted activists from the unregistered 'Atajurt' movement held a press conference alleging pressure and demanding the activists' release. Nurgul Ibrayeva, wife of movement leader Bekzat Maksutkhan, reported her husband's deteriorating health, including significant weight loss and wounds, and claimed that items sent to him are not accepted by the colony.

item.title: Kazakhstan to continue increasing salaries for 'Kazvodkhoz' employees
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to further increase the salaries of employees at 'Kazvodkhoz', the state water management enterprise. Current salaries have already been raised by 50 percent. These measures aim to attract qualified specialists, reduce staff turnover, and enhance professional levels within the water sector.

item.title: Taliban Trade Official Travels to India for Business Discussions
item.description: A deputy minister from the Taliban's Ministry of Industry and Trade has traveled to India at the official invitation of the Indian government. He will attend an international exhibition and meet with senior Indian officials, traders, and investors to discuss trade and economic cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Oversight of Car Wash Water Consumption
item.description: Kazakhstan will strengthen control over how car washes use drinking water. Businesses must install systems for water recycling and reuse. The Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation is working with inspection bodies to explain water legislation and expand the implementation of water reuse technologies.

item.title: Kazakhstan Uncovers Thousands of Hectares Under Illegal Irrigation
item.description: Since the beginning of the year, Kazakhstan has identified 96 cases of illegal water intake, affecting nearly 6,000 hectares of land. Fines totaling 189 million tenge have been levied. Legal proceedings are ongoing, and the use of satellite imagery and calculations aids in detecting such violations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Warns of Incitement to Ethnic Conflict Ahead of Elections
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov stated he received information about "malicious politicians" aiming to incite conflict between Uzbeks and Kyrgyz citizens ahead of elections. He urged citizens, especially elders, to prevent young people from being manipulated by provocateurs. Japarov encouraged reporting any suspicious activities to security agencies.

item.title: Kazakhstan Dismantles Criminal Group Selling Stolen Cars Abroad
item.description: Kazakh authorities have busted a criminal group that allegedly registered cars using fake identities and sold 56 vehicles abroad. The suspects reportedly used second-tier banks and microfinance organizations to secure loans for these vehicles before exporting and reselling them. Investigations are ongoing to recover the cars.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Develop its Own Space Industry by 2031
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is developing a state program for 2027-2031 to establish a national space industry. The initiative aims to integrate satellite technologies into governance, economy, and security, including creating remote sensing infrastructure and developing satellite communication and geoinformation technologies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Enhances Oncology Care with New Technologies and Equipment
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is advancing its oncology services by integrating modern medical technologies and equipment. The National Center for Oncology and Hematology will open a nuclear medicine department in 2025, featuring a SPECT scanner for early tumor detection. Mammography units with new functions are also being introduced, with specialists undergoing training.

item.title: Man Arrested in Uzbekistan for Growing and Selling Drugs
item.description: A man has been detained in the Tashkent region of Uzbekistan on suspicion of cultivating and selling drugs. Law enforcement found packaged doses and larger quantities hidden in jars at his home. The suspect is accused of illegally growing, processing, and distributing narcotics, facing up to 20 years in prison.

item.title: Iran Warns of Worsening Gas Shortages This Winter Due to War Damage
item.description: The Iranian government has warned of potential gas shortages this winter, exacerbated by damage to processing facilities from the ongoing conflict. Spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani stated that supply disruptions, including in the capital Tehran, are possible if consumption remains high. The projected shortage is estimated at 430 million cubic meters, up from 300 million previously.

item.title: Criminal Group Involved in Smuggling 56 Vehicles Abroad Exposed in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry has disrupted a criminal group suspected of car fraud and smuggling. The suspects used fake identities to register vehicles as collateral with banks and microfinance organizations, then exported and resold them abroad. 56 vehicles are believed to have been smuggled.

item.title: Man Shot Dead in Kunduz Province Amid Rising Insecurity
item.description: A man, identified as Sayed Nawab Mujaddidi, a hotel owner, was shot dead by two armed men in Kunduz city on Wednesday evening. The motive and circumstances remain unclear. This incident occurs as insecurity, targeted killings, and robberies have increased across Afghanistan in recent months.

item.title: US Asks Russia to Present New Security Proposal for Europe
item.description: The United States has requested Russia to submit a new proposal regarding a security agreement with Europe. The document should clearly outline steps Moscow will take to de-escalate tensions on the continent. This issue is set to be discussed during Kushner and Uitkoff's meeting with the Russian president.

item.title: Over Half of Kazakhs Interested in Politics But Doubt Influence, Survey Finds
item.description: A survey by DEMOSCOPE reveals that over half of Kazakhstan's residents follow public and political events, but nearly 45% believe citizens lack real influence on government decisions. Almost half of respondents did not participate in public life in the past year. Elections and referendums remain the most common form of participation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Social Fund Explains Low Pensions Despite Long Work History
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Social Fund Chairman explained that pension amounts depend not only on work experience but also on insurance contributions. Even with years of work, low or non-existent employer contributions result in smaller pensions. The fund operates on an insurance principle, meaning payouts vary based on individual contributions.

item.title: President Sadyr Japarov Warns of Strict Measures Against Election Incitement
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has issued a warning to the citizens of Kyrgyzstan regarding provocateurs aiming to incite ethnic conflict, particularly between Uzbeks and Kyrgyz, before the elections. He urged citizens to maintain unity and stated that strict measures will be taken against those attempting to divide the nation, recalling past conflicts in 1990 and 2010.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Increase Funded Pension Contributions
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering increasing the percentage of insurance contributions directed towards citizens' funded pensions. Currently at 2%, the Social Fund is exploring an increase but has not specified the exact amount or timeline for these reforms. The goal is to allow for greater accumulation of funds for future pension payments.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Increase Pension Payments for Certain Categories of Citizens from January 1
item.description: From January 1, 2027, Kyrgyzstan will increase pension payments and supplements for specific citizen groups. The Social Fund plans to allocate an additional 7.5 billion soms from the state budget for these purposes. The increase will affect mothers with the "Baatyr Ene" title, people with disabilities, and war veterans.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Simplifies Pension Application Process Through 'Tunduk' App
item.description: Over 6,000 Kyrgyz citizens have applied for pensions through the 'Tunduk' mobile app, eliminating the need for in-person visits. The Social Fund is also gradually increasing the minimum insurance period for pension eligibility. The app integrates with state databases, simplifying the collection of necessary information for applicants.

item.title: Tajikistan and Vietnam Discuss Joint Investment Projects in Key Sectors
item.description: Tajikistan's State Committee for Investments held meetings with Vietnamese officials to deepen economic dialogue and initiate investment projects. Both sides see potential in agricultural processing, textiles, construction materials, logistics, and digital technologies. They agreed to enhance interaction and information exchange on investment opportunities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Reviews Safety Protocols After Teenager's Tragic Mountain Death
item.description: Following the death of 14-year-old Amir Kunakunov in Al-Archa National Park, Kyrgyzstan is reviewing its emergency response and coordination systems. Serious shortcomings were identified, leading to dismissals and a criminal investigation into negligence. Experts emphasize the need for rigorous training and preparation for mountain activities to prevent future tragedies.

item.title: Russian Oil Refining Drops 30% Amidst Wave of Drone Attacks on Refineries
item.description: Russia's oil refining capacity has decreased by approximately 30% following a series of drone attacks on major refineries since late October. Nine out of 35 large refineries, with a combined capacity of 2.2 million barrels per day, have been affected. These attacks disrupt the domestic fuel market and pose risks to oil product exports.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Major Gas Processing Project in Atyrau Region by Year-End
item.description: A significant gas processing plant with a capacity of 1 billion cubic meters per year is set to launch in the Makat district of Atyrau region by the end of the year. The project, located at the Kashagan field, will produce commercial gas, liquefied petroleum gas, stable gas condensate, and granulated sulfur.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Top Officials Arrested on Corruption Charges
item.description: The heads of Kazakhstan's sovereign wealth fund 'Samruk-Kazyna' and national railway company 'Kazakhstan Temir Zholy' have been arrested on corruption charges. A political analyst commented that this demonstrates the principle of 'Law and Order', emphasizing that no one, regardless of their position, should be exempt from anti-corruption efforts. The analyst noted public expectation for strict measures against leaders managing vast state assets.

item.title: National Working Group Visits Turkistan to Promote President's Address
item.description: A national working group has arrived in the Turkistan region to explain President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address to the nation, titled "Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Period." The group includes members of the National Assembly, the People's Council, and deputy ministers of agriculture and water resources. They met with civil society representatives, academics, students, and healthcare workers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Updates Rules for Company Registration and Liquidation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has revised procedures for the state registration, re-registration, and termination of legal entities. Amendments clarify requirements for beneficial owner information, charter documentation, tax and customs debt checks, company reorganizations, and registry updates. The new rules aim to streamline business operations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Establishes Voluntary Pension Contributions for Citizens Abroad
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has launched a program allowing citizens living and working abroad to voluntarily pay insurance contributions. Through the "Tunduk" app, they can register and make payments. The Social Fund is also pursuing pension cooperation agreements with countries like China, Turkey, South Korea, Austria, and Germany.

item.title: Kazakh Ministry Assures No Risk to Drinking Water from Nuclear Plant Construction
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation stated that the construction of a nuclear power plant will not pose risks to drinking water. The Balkhash Lake region sources its drinking water from underground springs, while the plant will draw water from the lake itself. The ministry is also working to clean the Ili River, which feeds the lake.
